Let $u={log}_{3}⁡x.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡3}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡3\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $1$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $1$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{{log}_{3}⁡x}{x}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{3}{log}_{3}⁡x\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}u\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡3\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡3{\int }_{0}^{1}u\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡3\cdot \frac{{u}^{2}}{2}{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡3\cdot (\frac{{1}^{2}}{2}-\frac{{0}^{2}}{2}) \\  & =\frac{\operatorname{ln}⁡3}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
